children: NuRAN received a Nasdaq deficiency notice after its closing bid price stayed below $1.00 for 30 consecutive business days. It has until May 10, 2027 to regain compliance; the notice has no immediate effect on its listing.
Bid price below $1.00 for 30 business days
The deficiency puts continued Nasdaq listing at risk if the company does not cure it.
The closing bid must be at least $1.00 for 10 consecutive business days during the period.
Notice has no immediate effect on listing or trading
Shares remain listed for now; the notice is not a delisting decision.
Reverse split may be used to cure deficiency
A reverse split is a possible compliance measure, not an announced action.
Delisting possible if deficiency is not cured
If ineligible for more time or unable to cure, shares may be subject to delisting.

This is an initial Nasdaq compliance notice, not a delisting decision; the release reports the bid price was below the threshold for 30 consecutive business days. The next key milestone is whether the closing bid reaches $1.00 for 10 consecutive business days by May 10, 2027, or whether NuRAN qualifies for an additional compliance period.
from NuRAN Wireless Inc. distributed by ACCESS Newswire.
